generated_for: Project AEGIS-PHARMA V2 — governed agentic AI decision support
description: Machine-readable architecture graph of the repository: nodes (components), edges (real call/data relationships read from source), and flows (ordered end-to-end paths through the system). Built by reading the code, not from documentation.

nodes.label: Login
nodes.tooltip: Session entry point. AuthContext + RequireAuth wrap every other page; the operator's role is established here and carried as requester_role on every run.

nodes.label: Overview
nodes.tooltip: The ten-second read: pending queue, dependency health, recent runs. Every number comes from /api/dashboard or /api/queue — any metric the backend cannot supply renders 'Not available' rather than zero.

nodes.label: Decisions
nodes.tooltip: The approver's work queue. Opening an item shows DecisionSupport, DomainFindings, GovernanceChecks and the ApprovalPanel where the human decision is actually taken.

nodes.label: Run History
nodes.tooltip: Filterable history of every agent run with its terminal state, token cost and audit timeline. Backed entirely by the SQLite audit store.

nodes.label: Evidence Explorer
nodes.tooltip: Answers 'what does the corpus contain, and what may I rely on?' — deliberately shows untrusted and superseded documents that evidence.retrieve filters out, because hiding them would defeat the page's purpose.

nodes.label: Governance
nodes.tooltip: Live view of the policy register: 13 registered policies (P-01…P-13), their bound ADR/BC/hook, and which have an executable eval behind them.

nodes.label: Inject Coverage
nodes.tooltip: Maps each challenge inject (INJ-xxx) to the test or grader that covers it, and shows honestly which are uncovered.

nodes.label: Health
nodes.tooltip: Per-dependency health: Neo4j, Redis, audit store, LLM provider. Degraded and unavailable are distinct states — degraded mode is safe, not offline-capable (ADR-007).

nodes.label: Workflows
nodes.tooltip: Catalogue of the six governed workflows with their prohibitions stated verbatim — what each may do and what it may never do.

nodes.label: API Client
nodes.tooltip: Single typed fetch layer for the whole dashboard. Every page goes through it; nothing calls the API directly.

nodes.label: POST /api/runs
nodes.tooltip: The only way to start a governed run. Selects the workflow graph, mints a run_id, and executes the pipeline to its first interrupt or terminal state.

nodes.label: POST /api/runs/{id}/decide
nodes.tooltip: Records a human approve/reject/veto. This is where terminal authority actually lives — the graph can only ever propose.

nodes.label: GET /api/queue
nodes.tooltip: Runs currently interrupted and awaiting a named human approver.

nodes.label: GET /api/runs
nodes.tooltip: Paged run history, per-run detail, and filter facets — all read from the audit store, never recomputed.

nodes.label: GET /api/evidence
nodes.tooltip: Read-only evidence catalogue for humans. Structurally separate from the governed retrieval tool so a non-citable document can never reach a run.

nodes.label: GET /api/governance
nodes.tooltip: Policy register snapshot: which policies are registered, traced, and executably tested.

nodes.label: GET /api/evals/scorecard
nodes.tooltip: Latest eval scorecard across the 15 scenario files — the release-gate signal.

nodes.label: GET /api/coverage/injects
nodes.tooltip: Inject-to-test coverage map.

nodes.label: GET /api/dashboard
nodes.tooltip: Aggregated cost, guardrail-trip, terminal-state and cache-hit panels, computed from the audit store and Redis counters.

nodes.label: GET /api/health
nodes.tooltip: Liveness plus per-dependency detail.

nodes.label: batch_review
nodes.tooltip: GxP Batch Review. Reconciles genealogy, lab results, deviations, CAPA, validation state and release-packet completeness. Must NEVER release, reject, reprocess, relabel or recall a batch.

nodes.label: pv_intake
nodes.tooltip: PV Intake & Signal Support. Duplicate detection, terminology normalisation, reporting-clock reconstruction, listedness. Must NEVER make final seriousness, causality, expectedness, reportability or signal-confirmation decisions.

nodes.label: supply_planning
nodes.tooltip: Supply-Shortage & Cold-Chain Planning. Generates traceable, non-executing options. Must NEVER change inventory status, reserve, allocate, ship or initiate recall.

nodes.label: clinical_integrity
nodes.tooltip: Clinical trial data-integrity review. Added in Stage 21 following the identical governed pattern (ADR-008: one graph per workflow).

nodes.label: regulatory_completeness
nodes.tooltip: Regulatory submission completeness review. Same governed skeleton, different domain node.

nodes.label: research_review
nodes.tooltip: Research reconciliation review. Structural completeness and conflict findings only.

nodes.label: intake
nodes.tooltip: Creates GovernedState: run_id, workflow, requester_role, authorization_checked_at. Every downstream node reads and writes only this single state object (BC-9).

nodes.label: policy_load
nodes.tooltip: Loads the versioned policy contract. If it is unreachable the graph REFUSES — there is deliberately no cached-policy fallback (ADR-005, BC-3, P-05).

nodes.label: retrieve
nodes.tooltip: Calls evidence.retrieve. At most one scope-preserving broadening per run (G3), enforced by a server-side counter rather than caller bookkeeping.

nodes.label: evidence_gate
nodes.tooltip: Decides sufficient / broaden / abstain / defect_halt. A non-citable item reaching this point is a defect_halt, not a filter miss.

nodes.label: reconcile
nodes.tooltip: Domain node for batch, clinical, regulatory and research workflows. Produces structural findings and gaps — never a disposition.

nodes.label: duplicate_check
nodes.tooltip: PV-only. Surfaces duplicate candidates with matched_fields and reasons; an edge with a score but no reason fails its own contract.

nodes.label: normalize_terminology
nodes.tooltip: PV-only. Suggests controlled-vocabulary normalisations with the terminology source cited. Suggestions, never applied silently.

nodes.label: generate_options
nodes.tooltip: Supply-only. Drafts shortage options carrying no_side_effects — options are proposals, and nothing downstream can execute them.

nodes.label: synthesize
nodes.tooltip: The only node that calls a model. Output is constrained to DecisionSupportOutput, whose extra='forbid' means a disposition field cannot be attached even by a malformed node (ADR-004 layer 1).

nodes.label: guard1
nodes.tooltip: Prohibited-action guard, first pass — before the critic sees the draft. ADR-004 layer 3.

nodes.label: critic_verify
nodes.tooltip: Independent verification pass. Returns approve_for_human or reject with a closed-enum reason code; a retry is legitimate only if the code is retryable AND distinct from every prior code in the run.

nodes.label: guard2
nodes.tooltip: Prohibited-action guard, second pass — after the critic, because the critic's own feedback could reintroduce a banned signal. Also the cache-write point.

nodes.label: hitl_route
nodes.tooltip: Determines which named human roles must act, and how many legs of approval are required. Supply needs both legs — one leg is not approval.

nodes.label: hitl_interrupt
nodes.tooltip: LangGraph interrupt. The run stops here and waits for a real human; the checkpointer holds state until /decide resumes it.

nodes.label: blocked (prohibition)
nodes.tooltip: Terminal. Reached when the guard matches a prohibited signal. PROHIBITION_ADJACENT is the one reason code with no retry edge at all — retrying it would ask the model to rephrase a near-miss on the highest-severity control.

nodes.label: abstained (cap)
nodes.tooltip: Terminal. Retry or budget ceiling exceeded — the run abstains rather than continuing to spend.

nodes.label: finalize
nodes.tooltip: Writes the audit record and returns the contracted response. Every path — approved, blocked, abstained, refused — passes through here, so no run can complete unaudited.

nodes.label: evidence.retrieve
nodes.tooltip: Governed retrieval. Untrusted and superseded items are filtered inside the Cypher query itself — there is no code path that returns them and lets a caller decide. Currently matches terms against source_file and authority (no document body, no embeddings).

nodes.label: batch.reconcile
nodes.tooltip: Reconciles batch evidence into findings and gaps. Rejects any evidence_id it cannot trace to this run's own retrieval.

nodes.label: pv.duplicate_check
nodes.tooltip: Duplicate candidate detection with mandatory matched_fields.

nodes.label: pv.normalize_terminology
nodes.tooltip: Controlled-vocabulary suggestions with cited terminology source and version.

nodes.label: supply.generate_options
nodes.tooltip: Drafts non-executing supply options against a constraint set.

nodes.label: clinical.integrity_check
nodes.tooltip: Clinical data-integrity structural checks.

nodes.label: regulatory.completeness
nodes.tooltip: Submission completeness structural checks.

nodes.label: research.reconcile
nodes.tooltip: Research reconciliation structural checks.

nodes.label: policy_engine
nodes.tooltip: Loads and version-checks the policy contract. The one governance module every other module depends on — if it raises, the graph must refuse rather than proceed on a stale or default contract.

nodes.label: evidence_gate
nodes.tooltip: Sufficiency decision as a typed result, so an empty list can never be mistaken for 'sufficient'.

nodes.label: prohibited_action_guard
nodes.tooltip: ADR-004 layer 3. Pattern-matches generated text against the workflow's banned terms and field names. Known residual risk: a model complying with an injection without using a listed term is not caught.

nodes.label: hitl_route
nodes.tooltip: Tier clock: T1 reminder at 8h, T2 escalation at 16h, T3 expiry at 24h. Recording an approval after T3 is structurally impossible, not merely discouraged.

nodes.label: audit_store
nodes.tooltip: Append-only SQLite ledger: agent_run, human_override_recorded, hitl_escalation, hitl_expired, prohibited_action_blocked. Note: records policy_contract_version but not the model or prompt that produced the run.

nodes.label: response_cache
nodes.tooltip: Redis cache keyed on subject_id + evidence_ids. A hit whose evidence has since become superseded is treated as a miss, not served — the exact ADR-003 guardrail scenario.

nodes.label: pending_queue
nodes.tooltip: Holds interrupted runs awaiting their named human approver.

nodes.label: evidence_catalog
nodes.tooltip: Read-only human-facing catalogue. Deliberately returns untrusted and superseded items, and returns a different type than the governed path so a catalogue row cannot be passed off as retrieved evidence.

nodes.label: tool_manifest
nodes.tooltip: Declares which tools exist and what capabilities each may hold — ADR-004 layer 2, capability absence.

nodes.label: GovernedState
nodes.tooltip: The single state object every node reads and writes. Also defines the closed ReasonCode enum and which codes permit a retry.

nodes.label: payloads
nodes.tooltip: Per-workflow typed payloads with extra='forbid'. Layer 1 of the three-layer prohibition enforcement: a disposition field cannot be constructed at all.

nodes.label: EvidenceItem
nodes.tooltip: Only 'approved' and 'draft' are citable statuses. A superseded or untrusted item has no representable value here — construction would raise.

nodes.label: hitl_decision
nodes.tooltip: The human decision value object recorded against a run.

nodes.label: kg.ingest
nodes.tooltip: Ingests knowledge_catalog.csv into Neo4j as EvidenceItem nodes plus supersedes edges. Idempotent (MERGE). Implements 1 of the 16 node types and 1 of the 13 edge types the KG schema specifies.

nodes.label: kg.client
nodes.tooltip: Neo4j session management, with an explicit not-configured state so an unreachable graph surfaces as unavailable rather than an empty corpus.

nodes.label: llm_client
nodes.tooltip: Two providers behind one protocol, selected by LLM_PROVIDER. Both are prompted and parsed identically, so swapping providers is a constructor choice — not a prompt or parsing change.

nodes.label: redis_client
nodes.tooltip: Redis connection for the response cache.

nodes.label: observability
nodes.tooltip: Computes the cost, guardrail-trip, terminal-state and cache panels from real audit rows and Redis counters.

nodes.label: tool contracts (8)
nodes.tooltip: One JSON Schema per governed tool, defining input, output and the closed set of error codes. Contract tests assert the implementation matches.

nodes.label: policy_contract.v1
nodes.tooltip: Versioned prohibition contracts per workflow: banned terms and banned field names, injected at compile time and never agent-supplied.

nodes.label: policy register
nodes.tooltip: 13 policies (P-01…P-13), each traced to an ADR, bounded context or hook. Three HITL policies are flagged as having no executable eval yet.

nodes.label: Neo4j
nodes.tooltip: Knowledge graph. Currently holds 33 EvidenceItem nodes and their supersedes edges — a metadata catalogue, not yet the 16-type domain graph the schema specifies.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.tooltip: Response cache with supersession-aware invalidation.

nodes.label: Audit store
nodes.tooltip: The system of record for what happened: every run, every human override, every escalation, every prohibited-action block.

nodes.label: knowledge_catalog
nodes.tooltip: 33 governed documents with authority, effective date, status, trust, jurisdiction, supersedes and SHA-256. Includes deliberately untrusted fixtures (K-998, K-999) that must never become instructions.

nodes.label: Anthropic
nodes.tooltip: Route A (ADR-009). The only provider whose output counts as real evidence for the measurement gate.

nodes.label: Groq
nodes.tooltip: Dev-only substitute. Output is explicitly provisional — Stage 20a/20b results were measured here and still owe a Route A re-run.

nodes.label: eval runner
nodes.tooltip: Loads every scenario file, dispatches to its grader, compares actual against expected, emits a scorecard.

nodes.label: 15 scenario sets
nodes.tooltip: 63 scenarios across business outcome, evidence fidelity, GxP boundary, audit trail, injection, abstention, PV clocks, tool authorisation, privacy, subgroup, cost, model substitution and agent failure modes.

nodes.label: 12 graders
nodes.tooltip: One grader per concern — evidence authority, prohibited action, schema, audit trail, PV clocks, trajectory, security, privacy, subgroup, latency/cost, loop guard, cache correctness.

nodes.label: release gates
nodes.tooltip: Ship / no-ship gate. Failed critical gates block release.

nodes.label: test suites
nodes.tooltip: contract, integration, e2e, unit, security, performance, resilience — including the red-team suite that asserts document text is never transmitted to the model.

nodes.label: threat catalogue
nodes.tooltip: 12 catalogued threats with controls mapping and a residual-risk register that records what is genuinely still open.

nodes.label: abuse cases
nodes.tooltip: T-01 indirect prompt injection, T-06 evidence-authority bypass, T-11 denial of wallet — all three actually attempted against the live system, not just described.

nodes.label: SBOM
nodes.tooltip: 11 pinned runtime dependencies, verified against the installed environment by verify_sbom.py. Covers packages only — not models, prompts or tool contracts.

flows.name: Batch Review — approved by human
flows.summary: The full governed path for a GxP batch review that reaches a human approver and is approved. Note the terminal decision is taken at /decide by a named person — the graph only ever proposes.

steps.note: Versioned policy contract loaded, or refuse
Findings and gaps, never a disposition
Run stops and waits for a human

flows.name: Prohibited action blocked
flows.summary: A draft containing a banned signal (e.g. recommending batch release) is caught by the guard and terminates. PROHIBITION_ADJACENT has no retry edge at all — the system will not ask the model to rephrase a near-miss on its highest-severity control.

flows.name: Insufficient evidence → abstain
flows.summary: When evidence cannot support a finding, the system abstains rather than guessing. One scope-preserving broadening is permitted first, enforced server-side.

steps.note: Typed result, not a bare bool

flows.name: Critic rejects → bounded retry
flows.summary: The critic can send a draft back to synthesize, but only with a reason code that is retryable AND distinct from every prior code in the run. Exhausting the budget abstains rather than looping.

flows.name: Cache hit with supersession recheck
flows.summary: The ADR-003 guardrail scenario. A cached answer whose underlying evidence has since become superseded is treated as a miss, not served — verified against live Redis and live Neo4j.

steps.note: Stale entry counts as a miss

flows.name: PV Intake — duplicates, terminology, veto
flows.summary: PV adds duplicate detection and terminology normalisation before synthesis. Its distinguishing property: a veto forces rejected and is never overridden, tested against the live graph.

steps.note: Score without a reason fails its contract

flows.name: Supply Planning — dual approval
flows.summary: Supply generates non-executing options and requires two independent approval legs. One leg is explicitly not approval — implemented and tested, not just documented.

steps.note: Allocate / reserve / ship are banned signals

flows.name: HITL escalation → T3 expiry
flows.summary: The approval clock: reminder at 8h, escalation at 16h, expiry at 24h. Recording an approval after T3 raises rather than being quietly accepted — no action is the terminal state.

flows.name: Human decision recorded
flows.summary: Where terminal authority actually lives. The approver acts in the UI, the decision is written to the append-only ledger, and the run resumes from its checkpoint.

steps.note: Visible in history and audit timeline

flows.name: Knowledge ingest → graph
flows.summary: The 33-document governed corpus is loaded into Neo4j with authority, effective date, status and SHA-256. Only EvidenceItem nodes and supersedes edges are implemented — 15 further node types remain specified but unbuilt.

flows.name: Eval harness → release gate
flows.summary: 63 scenarios across 15 files, dispatched to 12 graders, producing a scorecard that gates release. Failed critical gates block ship.

steps.note: Dispatch each scenario to its grader

flows.name: Adversarial red-team path
flows.summary: Three of the twelve catalogued threats were actually attempted against the running system. T-01 targets the guard and retrieval; the residual risk that the guard is evadable by paraphrase is recorded rather than papered over.

steps.note: Red-team suite asserts doc text never reaches the model

flows.name: Observability → Overview
flows.summary: Every panel on the Overview page is computed from real audit rows and Redis counters. Any metric the backend cannot supply renders as 'Not available' rather than a misleading zero.

flows.name: Policy unreachable → refuse
flows.summary: There is deliberately no cached-policy fallback. If the policy contract cannot be loaded, the run refuses rather than proceeding on a stale or default contract (ADR-005, BC-3, P-05).

steps.note: Dependency shown as unavailable, not degraded
